items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] I've heard Eubie Blake and Earl Hines talk about learning music by listening...

ctx.x: And so I'm just listening -- that's when I first heard of "Jack the Bear" with Duke Ellington and Blanton. And so I knew a whole lot of the arrangements, and I knew a whole lot of tunes, just by listening. And the little 5 piece band I'm working with, we would play them -- "Jumping at the Woodside" and "One o'Clock Jump" -- even things the Ceford band was playing. Lanceford Luntzwood was very popular.
I've heard Eubie Blake and Earl Hines talk about learning music by listening, and how you have almost a photographic memory. All these tunes, it seems phenomenal, but that's how you learn.

You learn and you retain those tunes, you know? You never forget them. I mean, you might not play a tune for a year, but somebody will say, "Do you know so and so" - and he'll call the name; you can't remember the name, but as soon as he plays at least 3 or 4 bars, you know it and you can play it.
